name: TTP-WorkBench
description: TTP-WorkBench Artifact TTP-WorkBench is a framework and benchmark for executing and comparing ten tools from prior work that extract MITRE ATT&CK tactics, techniques, and procedures from cyber threat reports. The artifact contains standardized tool adapters, container build specifications, curated prior-work data, and 281 new threat reports for benchmarking the tools. Provided scripts automate the container builds, dataset compilation, functionality tests, reproduction experiments, and capacity-aware analysis. The artifact documentation gives a setup procedure and three evaluation exercises to demonstrate that the artifact is functional and reproducible. Paper Abstract In cybersecurity operations, threat reports are a valuable resource to understand emerging threats, with MITRE ATT&CK serving as a common framework for interpreting the attacker’s tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs) described in the reports. Manually inferring TTPs from textual reports is difficult and time-consuming, which has motivated dozens of prior studies in automated extraction and labeling approaches. However, there has been no comprehensive comparison across tools, perhaps because many open-source implementations are difficult to run, lack experimental artifacts, or do not perform well on new data. While others have pointed out these systemic obstacles to reproducibility in the broader security research community, we practically analyze and address them in the field of automated TTP extraction.
